subject: Datacore encryption & data handling — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Erin Chen <erin@datacore.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Datacore encryption & data handling — follow-up and next steps

Hi Erin — thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap of what we covered on the security/encryption front and the proposed next steps so we can align the procurement path.

Key points from the call (high level):
- PII scope: customer IDs and email addresses will be considered sensitive; Datacore confirmed tokenization is not in scope today but you may want to revisit for long-term retention minimization.
- Retention: you mentioned primary retention window of 90 days for inference inputs/outputs, but audit/log retention needs to be at least 12 months for compliance — please confirm if that is firm.
- Residency: initial deployment target is US East; EU-only residency option may be required for some subsidiaries.
- Logging: request for immutable access logs and admin audit logs with S3/Blob export and 1yr retention.
- Encryption: in-transit must be TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 preferred). At-rest should be AES-256. You asked specifically about customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM-backed keys — see options below.

Redwood options relevant to Datacore:
1) Hosted API + customer KMS integration: Redwood can call your cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure KeyVault) to encrypt model artifacts and symmetric data keys. This is the fastest route but requires an IAM trust path.
2) BYOK via EKM/HSM integration: we support integrating with external key managers (Cloud HSM or on-prem HSM) for key-wrap of at-rest keys. This provides HSM-backed roots and is the recommended pattern for customers requiring FIPS/HSM attestations.
3) Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem): for the most restrictive deployments we can ship a private control plane and integrate local HSM appliances; this gives you full network isolation and direct HSM control.

Tradeoffs and practical notes:
- Latency: BYOK key unwrap operations happen at key rotation time — per-token latency impact is typically negligible (most crypto ops are cached), though initial calls to unwrap may add single-digit ms. We'll provide measured numbers from similar customers in the security call.
- Logs & attestations: we can provide SOC 2 report excerpts and an encryption architecture diagram; the SOC 2 report is sensitive but available under NDA / via secure upload.
- Minimum data residency: we can pin model hosting to a region and replicate logs to your audit S3 in region if needed.

Proposed next steps (please confirm the items and owners):
- Security deep-dive call (technical) — propose Fri 2026-11-26 10:00 AM ET (Soojin + Marissa + Redwood infra security engineer).
- Share the security questionnaire (you mentioned you have one) — you can attach it or we can upload to a secure link.
- Draft SOW & procurement path — I attached a very small draft SOW (Datacore_SOW_v1.pdf) to start procurement discussion; Marissa will lead on commercials.

If anything above is mis-specified, tell me now and I’ll correct before the security call. Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the finish line quickly.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Erin Chen <erin@datacore.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-22T12:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Datacore encryption & data handling — follow-up and next steps

Thanks Soojin — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Retention: the 90 days for inference payloads is correct, but we require 12 months for audit/log retention. That is a firm requirement for the compliance team.
- Keys: we specifically require an HSM-backed root for customer-managed keys (we currently use AWS CloudHSM behind AWS KMS). Integrations that only rely on software-managed keys will not meet our policy.
- Residency: core inference must be US-East for now; however our legal team may require EU-only for a subset of traffic later — confirm whether the Redwood Private option can be configured EU-only.
- Evidence: please share SOC 2 Type II report (redacted ok) and an encryption architecture diagram prior to the security call.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) What is the expected latency delta when using your BYOK/HSM integration vs your standard hosted path? Any quant numbers from prior customers would help our perf team.
2) Can you support immutable, exportable admin and access logs for a 12 month retention? Are there any additional costs or storage limits?

I have attached our security questionnaire (Datacore_security_questions_filled.xlsx).

Proposed: confirm security call Fri 11/26 10:00 AM ET and include your infra security lead. Procurement contact is procurement@datacore.io — please route the SOW there when updated.

—Erin
Erin Chen
Security & Compliance Lead, Datacore Systems
erin@datacore.io

Attachments: Datacore_security_questions_filled.xlsx (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Erin Chen <erin@datacore.io>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Datacore encryption & data handling — follow-up and next steps

Erin — thanks for the specificity, that helps. Quick answers while Soo pulls security into the thread: 

- Latency: in our experience integrating customer KMS/HSM for key-wrap/unwrap adds negligible per-request latency thanks to KV cache of unwrapped data keys; measurable token-generation latency delta we’ve seen ranges from ~0.5–4ms depending on model and request size. We will run a short benchmark against your expected max sequence length during the security call.
- Logs: yes, we support immutable admin and access logs. We can stream logs to your S3 (or to a customer-managed logging account) and configure lifecycle policies for 12 months. There may be incremental storage cost; we’ll include an estimate in pricing.
- HSM support: we support AWS CloudHSM & external HSMs via EKM; for AWS CloudHSM we can establish an IAM-role and grant selective key usage for wrap/unwrap. For on-prem HSMs we use standard KMIP/EKM integrations.

I’ve uploaded a short SOW skeleton to route to procurement and included the technical appendix pointer — will send the DocuSign link after the security call so we have the integration approach captured.

Proposed attendees for Fri 11/26 call: Soo (AE), Marissa (Solutions), Rahul (Infra Sec) — Rahul will present the KMS/HSM options and run through an architecture diagram. Rahul is internal but I’ll confirm his availability.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Lead Solutions Engineer
